sentences.text:
Both appeals arise out of the judgment and award dated 12.01.2022 passed in MVC.No.111/2021 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hubballi (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2. Parties herein are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. The brief facts of the claim petition are as follows:

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hubballi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On 2nd day of September, 2020, at 4:40 p.m.,
Punit Malammanavar, the son of petitioner, was traveling on a motorcycle with registration No.
KA-63/K-9011 from Hubballi towards Kundagol on the Hubli-Laxmeshwar road.
At that time, a tipper lorry bearing No.KA-20/AA-6263 approached from the opposite direction at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and collided with the motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, the motorcycle rider sustained severe injuries and tragically passed away at the scene.

The petitioner further states that prior to the accident, her son was in good health, aged approximately 25 years on the date of the accident, and worked as a driver, earning a monthly salary of Rs.20,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB along with additional allowances.
Due to the accident, the petitioner suffered the loss of her earning family member, as well as emotional and financial hardships.
Consequently, the petitioner seeks compensation from the respondents.

In response to the notice,
respondent No.1 was served but remained absent and was declared as an ex-parte respondent.

Respondent No.2, represented by its advocate, filed a statement of objection, arguing that the driver of the lorry (the offending vehicle) did not possess a valid driving license, and therefore, the Insurance Company should not be held liable to pay compensation.
Furthermore, it is contended that the deceased himself did not hold a valid driving license, and thus, the Insurance Company should not be liable for compensation.
Additionally, it is argued that the owner and insurer of the motorcycle should also be considered as necessary parties in the petition.
It is asserted that the motorcycle rider was driving in a rash and negligent manner, and the accident resulted from a head-on collision.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 requests the dismissal of the petition with costs.

4. On the basis of rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:-
NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Padmavati W/O Basavaraj ...

3 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 02.09.2021 at 4-04 p.m. when deceased Punit Malammanavar (son of the petitioner) was proceeding from Hubli towards Kundagol on Hubli-Laxmeshwar road near Sherewad village on his motorcycle bearing No.KA- 63/K-9011, then the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-20/AA- 6263 came from Kundagol towards Hubballi i.e. from opposite side of motorcycle in high speed, rash or negligent manner and caused accident to the motorcycle and because of the accident, the motor cyclist died on the spot and said accident occurred due to fault of driver of the respondent No.1?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the said accident occurred due to fault of the motor cyclist and deceased had no any driving licence and hence, it is not liable to pay compensation, as pleaded in para No.6 of the objection?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?
4. What award or order?
5. To prove the case of petitioner, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to 10.

On closure of petitioner's side evidence, Insurance Company examined one witness as R.W.1 and got marked authorization certificate as Ex.R.1.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB 6.

On hearing the arguments, the Tribunal has given its findings to the above issues as under :
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : In the Negative.
Issue No.3 : Affirmative in part.
Issue No.4 : As per final order,
7. In view of the above findings, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.16,57,600/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

8. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the Insurance Company has preferred the appeal in MFA.No.101981/2022 questioning its liability to pay compensation and claimant has also filed appeal in MFA.No.101124/2022 for enhancement of compensation.
SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF INSURANCE COMPANY 9.
The learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company argues that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident.
Specifically, it is mentioned that the driver's license for a transport vehicle had expired on August 30, 2020, and it was renewed only on October 9, 2020.
However, the accident NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB occurred on September 2, 2020.
Therefore, it is evident that on the date of the accident, the driver did not hold a valid driving license to operate a transport vehicle.

The counsel contends that the Tribunal United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Padmavati W/O Basavaraj ... on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14207284/
4 did not take into consideration the defense raised by the Insurance Company and, for these reasons,
requests that the appeal be allowed.

10. To substantiate his argument, learned counsel for Insurance Company has relied on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court passed in Civil Appeal No.4749/2008 (arising out of SLP(c)
No.17920/2006) Ram Babu Tiwari vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and Others.

entities.text: Ram Babu Tiwari vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF APPELLANT-CLAIMANT.
11. The learned counsel representing the appellant- claimant asserts that the Tribunal correctly held the Insurance Company liable to pay compensation.

However, regarding the actual award of compensation, it is argued that the Tribunal did not grant a just and proper amount in accordance with the law, facts, and the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
On these grounds, the counsel seeks an increase in the compensation amount.

After hearing the arguments from both sides and reviewing the records, the following points require our consideration:
1.
Whether the appellant/Insurance Company has provided sufficient grounds to challenge the Tribunal's judgment and award concerning its liability.

2. Whether the appellant-claimant is entitled to an enhancement of compensation.
3. What the final order or award should be.
13. Our findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No. 1 is answered in the negative.
Point No. 2 is partly affirmed.
Point No. 3 will be addressed in the final order.
14. We have thoroughly reviewed the evidence and documentation presented in this case.
It is undisputed that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent actions of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The sole defense put forth by the Insurance Company is that the LMV (Light Motor Vehicle) driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle was valid from September 23,
2017, and remained in force until September 29, 2028.

The Insurance Company's defense NC:
2023:KHC-D:11043-DB centers on the fact that the LMV (transport license) was not renewed at the time of the accident.

However, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in AIR 2017 SC 3668, the defense raised by the Insurance Company cannot be accepted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.
We find no legal irregularities or infirmities regarding the liability imposed on the Insurance Company.
Therefore, we answer point No. 1 in the negative.
15. Point No.2:

With regard to quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,500/- per month, which is not in consonance with the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
In view of the said chart, Tribunal has to be considered the monthly notional income of the deceased at Rs.13,750/-.
In view of Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121, the age of deceased was 25 years, hence '18' multiplier is applicable.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% of the income has to be added as future prospects of the deceased and 50% has to be deducted as personal and living expenses of the deceased, then loss of dependency comes to (Rs.13,750/- + (40% Rs.5,500/-) - 50%
= Rs.9,625/-) Rs.9,625/- X 12 X 18 = Rs.20,79,000/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled for enhancement in loss of dependency.
16.

Keeping in mind the decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Sarla Verma's and Pranay Sethi's (supra), it is just and appropriate to award compensation as under :
1. Loss of dependency.
For love and affection.
For funeral expenses.
For loss of estate. Rs.16,500/-
17 . Accordingly, petitioner is entitled for enhancement of compensation.
Hence, we answer point No.2 in the partly affirmative.
18. Point No.3:

For the aforesaid discussions and reasons, we proceed to pass the following :
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11043-DB ORDER (i) Appeal filed by the Insurance Company in MFA.No.101981/2022 is dismissed.

(iii) Appellant-claimant is entitled for enhanced  compensation of Rs.21,56,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization as against Rs.16,57,600/- with interest at 6% per annum awarded by the Tribunal.
(iv) Insurance Company shall deposit the above said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment before the Tribunal.
